lessons.goal: 從人物對物品的態度變化理解對比與象徵。

questions.evidence: Lena's umbrella develops a small tear just before a week of rain. She wants to replace it, but her older brother offers to sew on a waterproof patch from his repair kit. The only patch he has is bright yellow, while the umbrella is dark blue.
options: It has a small tear.
It cannot be opened at all.
Its handle is missing.
Its frame is completely broken.
questions.prompt: What is wrong with Lena's umbrella?

questions.explanation: 黃補片與深藍傘面形成明顯對比。
options: It is the same color as the fabric.

questions.explanation: 一群藍傘中，她能靠補片立即辨識自己的傘。
options: It changes the weather.
It makes every blue umbrella waterproof.

questions.prompt: How does the yellow patch become useful beyond covering the tear?

questions.evidence:
Lena's umbrella develops a small tear just before a week of rain. She wants to replace it, but her older brother offers to sew on a waterproof patch from his repair kit. The only patch he has is bright yellow, while the umbrella is dark blue.

Lena worries that the repair will look strange. She agrees to try it because the frame and handle are still sound. Her brother explains what he can fix, and they test the repaired area with water before she carries it outside.

At school, a friend says the yellow shape looks like a little sun. Later, when several blue umbrellas crowd the stand, Lena finds hers immediately. The mark she wanted to hide has become both useful and personal.

She does not decide that every broken object should always be repaired. This umbrella had a small problem that the available method could solve. By Friday, she is no longer comparing it with a perfect new one. She likes the story of its repair and the bright shape that made it hers.
questions.explanation: 補片既修復功能，也成為物品的獨特故事。
options: A workable repair can add personal value to an object.
A repaired item must look exactly new to be useful.
Visible repairs always make belongings less desirable.
Every damaged object should be kept regardless of function.
questions.prompt: Which statement best fits Lena's final view?

lessons.story:
Lena's umbrella develops a small tear just before a week of rain. She wants to replace it, but her older brother offers to sew on a waterproof patch from his repair kit. The only patch he has is bright yellow, while the umbrella is dark blue.

Lena worries that the repair will look strange. She agrees to try it because the frame and handle are still sound. Her brother explains what he can fix, and they test the repaired area with water before she carries it outside.

At school, a friend says the yellow shape looks like a little sun. Later, when several blue umbrellas crowd the stand, Lena finds hers immediately. The mark she wanted to hide has become both useful and personal.

She does not decide that every broken object should always be repaired. This umbrella had a small problem that the available method could solve. By Friday, she is no longer comparing it with a perfect new one. She likes the story of its repair and the bright shape that made it hers.
lessons.title: The Umbrella with the Bright Patch
